title.narrative: Strategic Partnership CHD 2019-2022

description.narrative: A multi-annual strategic partnership between the Netherlands Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Centre for Humanitarian Dialogue (HD) which enables HD to respond rapidly and appropriately to developing political and violent crises and opportunities. The partnership provides the MFA with valued activities in mediation around the world and in regions of priority interest to the Netherlands while opening up networks more readily available to an independent, private actor.

title.narrative: 2.1.1 % coverage by HD projects and assessments of those countries affected by highly violent conflicts (HD indicator)

description.narrative: Percentage of coverage is based on HD's engagement in countries affected by highly violent conflicts, as listed by the Conflict Barometer published by the Heidelberg Institute. HD also engages in conflicts not on this list, either because they have escalated, are classified as frozen or protracted conflicts, or because HD engages in preventive action.

comment.narrative: In 2019, HD covered 80% of all countries affected by violent conflict
In 2021, HD covered about 81% of countries affected by highly violent political conflicts.
No target value was set for 2023

The publication of the Heidelberg conflict barometer for 2023 was delayed. This year's actual value is thus an estimate based on the 2022 Heidelberg conflict barometer. It's also important to note that the methodology for this indicator has changed since last year. Previously, HD's coverage of individual countries was considered. Now, the value expressed HD's coverage of conflicts. This (partly) explains the lower number.
70% of highly violent political conflicts (per 2020 Heidelberg Conflict Barometer)

title.narrative: 3.1.1 Support to strengthen third-party mediation in peace processes aimed at reaching inclusive peace agreements

description.narrative: NL MFA Security and Rule of Law results framework - output

title.narrative: 3.1 No. and % of conflicts that are addressed and resolved by community structures by the programme (ARC indicator) 1.1.1 Number of local conflicts mediated or supported (HD indicator)

comment.narrative: 82 local level agreements
161 local level agreements
No target value was set for 2023

HD’s local mediation is mainly focused in the Sahel and in the Philippines. Across the Sahel in 2023, HD’s networks of agro-pastoral mediators mediated conflicts at the local level across Mali, Niger, Burkina Faso, Mauritania and Chad, resolving more than 340 conflicts of competition for access rural natural resources. HD also facilitated 6 conventions or mechanisms aiming at regulating natural resource sharing across the Sahel. HD’s agro-pastoral mediators’ networks and peace structures further resolved 29 agro-pastoralist conflicts in the Central African Republic and 14 conflicts between farmers and herders in Togo. In Mali, 46 conflicts were resolved by HD’s religious mediators’ networks. In the Philippines, HD works with a local subsidiary in Sulu, Tumikang Sama-Sama Inc. (TSS). In 2023, TSS mediated 29 clan conflicts, out of which 9 conflicts were settled. In Maguindanao, HD supported Bangsamoro Mediators Inc., which mediated two conflicts, one of which was settled. HD also supported a group of volunteer mediators in the six acknowledged Moro Islamic Liberation Front camps in Mindanao. These volunteers mediated six cases, one of which was settled.

In 2020, HD successfully mediated or supported the resolution of at least 451 local conflicts, most of these in Francophone Africa. HD facilitated and supported 6 local peace agreements and the resolution of 435 local agro-pastoral conflicts across Togo and the Sahel region. In the Philippines, HD’s subsidiary in Sulu mediated 17 cases of clan conflict, helping the parties involved reach a formal settlement in 8 of them, and two ceasefires.
20 local agreements

In Africa, HD’s networks of mediators mediated micro-conflicts across Mali, Niger, Burkina Faso, Mauritania, Chad, Togo, and Central African Republic. In the Sahel, 385 agro-pastoral conflicts were resolved and 4 local agreements or mechanisms for natural resource sharing established. In Central African Republic, 51 agro-pastoral conflicts were resolved. In Togo, HD’s networks and peace structures further resolved 30 agro-pastoralist conflicts and 11 land conflicts. In Mali, 27 conflicts were prevented or resolved by HD’s networks of local-level mediators, in addition to 13 conflicts resolved by HD’s religious mediators’ networks. In the Philippines, HD’s subsidiary in Sulu mediated 40 clan conflicts. A formal settlement was reached in 13 conflicts, most of which were peace covenants.
400 local-level agreements

In the Sahel, HD mediated conflicts at the local level across Mali, Niger, Burkina Faso, Mauritania, Chad and Central African Republic. This work led to the resolution of 464 agro-pastoral conflicts, and 3 local agreements for the peaceful exploitation of disputed natural resources in Chad and Mali. HD’s network of religious mediators in Mali prevented or resolved 19 conflicts. In CAR, HD’s three cross-border networks on the border with Cameroon resolved 109 agro-pastoral conflicts. In the Philippines, HD’s subsidiary in Sulu mediated 26 cases of clan conflict between January and December 2021. Following this mediation, a formal settlement was reached in five conflicts.

title.narrative: No. of dialogue processes to strengthen the political/public debate (No of HD dialogue initiatives that include a public dialogue component)

comment.narrative: There were not target values set for 2023

HD is not a public advocacy organisation, but much of HD’s work tries to contribute and strengthen the political debate or discreetly influence policy or peace process design in local, national and sometimes regional contexts the scenes. Sometimes this includes a specific focus on strengthening the public debate, but will more often be in the form of discreet advisory services to conflict parties, facilitating dialogue with key stakeholders and experts, and sometimes as mediators between conflict parties. In 2023, the number of HD projects that included a public dialogue component was 26 (15 in Africa, 1 in Eurasia, 4 in Middle East and North Africa, and 4 in Asia, plus 2 global/cross-cutting projects).

HD is not a public advocacy organisation, but much of HD’s work tries to contribute and strengthen the political debate or discreetly influence policy or peace process design in local, national and sometimes regional contexts the scenes. Sometimes this includes a specific focus on strengthening the public debate, such as HD’s work on preventing COVID-19 related misinformation, but will more often be in the form of discreet advisory services to conflict parties, facilitating dialogue with key stakeholders and experts, and sometimes as mediators between conflict parties. In 2021, the number of HD projects that include a public dialogue component was 26 (14 in Africa, 2 in Eurasia, 3 in Middle East and North Africa, and 6 in Asia, plus 1 global/cross-cutting project).
In 2019, the number of HD projects that include a public dialogue component was 27 (14 in Africa, 1 in Eurasia, 3 in Middle East and North Africa, and 9 in Asia).
In 2020, the number of HD projects that include a public dialogue component was 25 (12 in Africa, 1 in Eurasia, 3 in Middle East and North Africa, and 9 in Asia).

In 2022, the number of HD projects that include a public dialogue component was 26 (15 in Africa, 1 in Eurasia, 4 in Middle East and North Africa, and 4 in Asia, plus 2 global/cross-cutting projects).
